lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Boston, 1920. A line of people wraps around the block.
lines.shot_hint: night street, crowd queue, place tag BOSTON 1920

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: They're waiting to hand a stranger their savings.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Fifty percent profit in forty-five days.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: His name became the word for this scam. The trick still hunts your money today.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Charles Ponzi said he'd found a loophole in the mail.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Buy postal reply coupons cheap in Europe. Cash them in America for more.

lines.speaker: INVESTOR
lines.text: So where's my money right now?

lines.speaker: PONZI
lines.text: Working. In coupons. Come back in forty-five days.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Around fifteen million dollars poured in.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: But here's the strange part. Almost none of it bought coupons.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: His plan needed 160 million coupons. About 27,000 existed.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Then the Boston Post started asking questions. It all collapsed.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Ponzi pleaded guilty to mail fraud. The newspaper won a Pulitzer.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: That was his problem. Here's yours.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: The SEC's red flags: guaranteed high returns. Returns that never dip. A seller who isn't registered.
lines.shot_hint: day lesson board, three flags pop in

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Before you invest, look them up at investor dot gov.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: A century later, the line is still there. It just moved online.
lines.shot_hint: back to the night street, queue now holding phones

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Would you have stood in that line?
